title: Covering for Andrew Brown and moving to tenor
summary: When Andrew Brown falls sick Thomas takes his solos on tenor, and the band diplomatically reassigns Brown to alto and Thomas to tenor.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: But let me back up. So where we got our big break was when Duke Ellington went to California to do the picture Three Little Words. So they chose our band to replace him. See, Mills was managing both bands, so it was kind of easy. But it was easy, too, because the Cotton Club was crazy about our band anyway, because The Missourians had been in the Cotton Club before and done a good job. So we got this job in the Cotton Club.

And one day, Brown got sick. Something was wrong, and he couldn't come to work. And he'd left his horn there. And they're playing, ain't got but two altos. And I said, "Listen, let me play the tenor." Because somehow or another, I had played tenor. I'd played all the horns. See, one horn didn't make no difference. And see, I learned how to play what little Jazz I could play with them bands out there in Minneapolis and North Dakota. So I picked up the saxophone and I started playing the solos better than

I'd been listening all the time he was playing. Because Brown was a little from the old school, he was a little on the corny side. But I'd heard Lester Young and Chu Berry and all them guys, and I had that modern way of playing. So I picked up the tenor and I started to play the solo -- the guys couldn't understand how I could play them (?). At one time, I could play anything I heard. If I heard the chord, I could play it. So sitting there and playing with a guy, you dug what the chord was.

So when Brown came back, they talked Brown into the idea that he sounded better on alto than I did. They didn't say I sounded...because they didn't want... Because see, Brown was one of the original guys in the Missourians, and They didn't want to insult him. So they switched it around to "You sound better on the alto than Walter does, and we'll let him play tenor." And that was the beginning of me playing tenor. That's how I got on the tenor.
